column2: req_desc

Keyboard authoring journey.
From a grading world's `draft` guide open in the editor, the author adds a step, chooses its parts, sets its apart amount, saves a version, moves the step and resizes the panes using only the keyboard, while the author's second tab shows the new version number live.

Editor toolbar Tab order.
Tab walks the `Editor tools` toolbar in exactly the numbered order published in Interactions, and Shift+Tab walks it backwards.

Add step and choose parts by keyboard.
Pressing Enter on `Add step` puts focus in the new step's title field and announces the addition in `Editor status`, and Space in the `Parts in this step` group sets that step's focus parts.

Apart slider applies after its delay.
Arrow keys on `Apart amount` leave `data-explode` unchanged until the editor apply delay in Motion and effects has fully passed, and change it exactly then.

Save shortcut from any control.
Ctrl+S or Cmd+S from a step text field saves a version without opening the browser's save dialog, announces the saved copy from Feedback states in `Editor status`, and updates `Latest version` in the author's second tab live.

Step move and pane separator by keyboard.
Alt+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowDown move the focused step and announce the move, and the `Resize stage and steps` separator follows the keys and value range published in Interactions, resizing the panes at once.

Typed limits keep the text.
Guide titles and step text accept exactly their published limit counted in code points with an emoji as one, and one more is refused with the copy naming the limit in `Editor status`, with the typed text still in the field after the notice has cleared.

Undo and redo journey.
With author and co-author in one draft in two browser contexts, the author undoes and redoes a text edit and a step move while the co-author's edit stays in place, and then saves the undone state as a version.

Undo restores own step text.
Ctrl+Z restores the author's last step-text edit character for character, Ctrl+Shift+Z brings it back, and each is announced with the undo and redo templates and labels from Feedback states.

Undo of a step move.
Undoing a step move restores the previous step order in the page and in the working-copy API and announces the move's label.

Undo spares a co-author's edit.
The author's undo never reverts an edit made by the co-author, as checked in both browser contexts and through the working-copy API, and an edit the co-author has since overwritten gives the cannot-undo copy.

Guide total follows price edits.
Changing `Unit price` updates `data-figure="total-cost"` in place from the server's reply with no reload and announces the guide total copy, and undo returns the earlier figure the same way.

Shortcuts on toolbar focus and empty stacks.
Undo and redo shortcuts work while a toolbar button has focus, and an empty stack gives the nothing-to-undo and nothing-to-redo copy from Feedback states.

Saving the undone state.
After an undo, Ctrl+S stores a version whose JSON holds the undone values and not the undone edit.

Scroll reading journey.
A reader of the world's `public` guide scrolls through all steps and back, and the stage hooks, counter, spoken progress and running cost follow the published scroll mapping both ways, ending at the closing total.

Scroll position sets the step.
Each scroll range in the published mapping sets `data-step`, the `Step counter` text and the `Reading progress` announcement for that step.

Apart amount follows the band.
Within a step's section `data-explode` rises or falls linearly through the published band, holds outside it, returns exactly on scrolling back, and the camera matrices drawn by the stage differ between steps with different poses.

Parts cost counts both ways.
On each change of current step `data-figure="parts-cost"` shows values strictly between old and new during its count, the exact final text at the end of the published duration, and counts downward when going back.

Header figures count up.
On opening a guide without a step address, the header figures count up over the published duration and end at the exact seeded text.

Stage keys orbit and zoom.
On the focused `Model stage` the keys in the keyboard table change `data-yaw`, `data-pitch` and `data-zoom` by the published amounts within their clamps, Home returns to the step's saved pose, and Tab leaves the stage.

Reader layouts and own-origin loading.
At each published viewport the reader shows the published stage and steps geometry with no sideways overflow and every callout inside the viewport, and every request the page makes goes to the app's own origin.

Apart at the Step look.
Each guide phase is a flat full-height field in its published colour butted against the next, the transparent stage holds still in front of the passing edge, non-focus parts are flat silhouettes in the field's text colour, and focus parts show their own materials with an opposing outline.

Waterline hero.
The home page opens with the published bone-over-red waterline headline, cut by the seam in two colours, with the wordmark, the solid slate link and the one supporting sentence and no image.

Stage built on bundled three.js.
The source renders the stage with three.js installed as a dependency, bundled and served from the app's own origin, with bundled font files and no remote code, font, image or model.

Deep link journey.
Starting from a world in two browser contexts, a step address opens settled, reading updates the address, Back and reload keep the place, signing in returns to the same step, and a second context cannot reach the private guide.

Step address opens settled.
Opening `?step=<n>` shows step n with its seeded `data-explode`, saved pose and final figures on first paint and no tween, and a reload keeps that step.

Address follows reading.
Scrolling replaces the address with the current `?step=<n>` and adds no history entry, while `Previous step`, `Next step` and step links add an entry, so Back returns to the previous step without a reload.

Step past the end.
A step number beyond the last opens the last step and shows the exact past-the-end notice from Feedback states.

Sign-in returns to the step.
`Ask the author` while signed out goes to the sign-in page with a local return path and, after signing in with the published controls, comes back to that exact path and step.

Non-local return lands on the dashboard.
A return address that is an absolute URL, starts with two slashes or a backslash pair, or carries a scheme lands on `/dashboard` after sign-in.

Private guide hidden from others.
The owner sees the world's `private` guide, while a signed-out context and the `reader` context get the not-found answer at the reader, embed, API, versions, forks and model routes, and it never appears in search.

Reduced motion journey.
Under reduced motion a reader moves through the `public` guide by buttons with every pose and figure final at once, and with WebGL off the same journey runs on stills.

Step buttons replace scrolling.
Under reduced motion `Previous step` and `Next step` change `data-step` and the step text, announce `Reading progress`, and scrolling the page never changes the step.

Pose snaps with no animation.
Under reduced motion a step change sets the hooks at once, no animations run on the stage or figures, and the camera matrices are final on the next drawn frame.

Figures final at once.
Under reduced motion every `data-figure` shows its exact final text immediately on load and on each step change, with no value in between.

Still fallback without WebGL.
With WebGL unavailable the stage has `data-state="still"`, an image named by the published template, the step text beside it, and the exact still-fallback copy in `Stage status`.

Still follows the step buttons.
With WebGL unavailable `Next step` changes the still's accessible name and image and the step text together.

Reduced motion controls fit a thumb.
At 375x812 under reduced motion, `Previous step` and `Next step` are at least 44 by 44 px and the page has no sideways overflow.

Phone journey.
At 375x812 with touch, a reader scrolls past the stage, uses `Free look` and reads the `Parts` list, and an author edits and saves in the `Editor panes` tabs while their desktop context sees the edit live.

Editor panes on a phone.
At 375x812 the `Editor panes` tabs show one pane at a time by touch and arrow keys, with the other panes out of the accessibility tree and Tab order.

Numbered parts list replaces callouts.
At 375x812 the reader shows the numbered `Parts` list of the current step's focus parts under the stage and shows no floating callouts.

Vertical drag scrolls the page.
With `Free look` off, a one-finger vertical drag on the stage scrolls the page and leaves `data-yaw` and `data-pitch` unchanged.

Free look orbits and pinches.
With `Free look` on, a one-finger drag on the stage changes `data-yaw` and `data-pitch` without scrolling the page, and a two-finger pinch changes `data-zoom`.

Phone edit reaches the desktop live.
A step text edit committed in the phone editor and saved there appears in the author's desktop context within the published live delay and without a reload.

Phone and tablet geometry.
At 375x812 and 768x1024 the reader and editor match the published layouts, with no sideways overflow and every control at least 44 by 44 px.

Model upload journey.
An author previews `bike-hub.glb` by drop, chooses a file by keyboard and uploads it, sees it confirmed as stored, sees refusals on the `short-limits` instance, and sees the outage copy on the `storage-down` instance.

Drop preview stays in the browser.
Dropping a valid .glb on the editor stage sets `data-state="preview"`, draws the model (draw calls and vertex buffer bytes rise), shows the exact previewing copy, and sends no request to the server.

Choosing a file by keyboard.
`Choose a model file` opens the file picker by Enter or Space as the alternative to drop, gives the same preview, and `Upload model` then reports upload progress in `Stage status`.

Stored only after MinIO confirms.
An upload shows the stored copy only after MinIO confirms length and checksum, the object at the published key is byte-identical to the file, and a replacement keeps every part with missing ones listed as unbound, as qualified in Business rules.

Upload refusals name the reason.
On `short-limits`, a renamed text file, a file one byte over `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, a model with `MODEL_MAX_PARTS` plus one parts and a model with an outside URI each show their exact refusal in `Stage status`, answer the published status and body, and store nothing, while files exactly at the limits are accepted.

Storage outage for authors.
On `storage-down` an upload shows the author outage copy and answers the published 503 body, saving text still works, publishing is refused with its copy, and health answers as published.

Storage outage for readers.
On `storage-down` the reader page of a world made on the primary shows the exact reader outage copy with the step text, parts and costs intact and `data-state="error"`.

Credentials from the environment.
The source reads every service credential and URL from the published environment variables at start, and no credential is hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Versions journey.
The author opens `Versions`, compares two seeded versions by keyboard, restores an older one through its dialog and sees the new version in a second tab, and the compare stays open while notices expire.

Picking versions by keyboard.
Tab reaches each `Version <n>` checkbox in the `Versions` region, Space picks it, and `Compare` opens the `Version compare` region for the two picked versions.

Compare labels and cost difference.
The compare lists steps in the published order labelled exactly by the published four words, marks removed and added words with words and a side bar as well as colour, and shows the seeded cost difference text.

Restore dialog by keyboard.
`Restore version <n>` opens its dialog by keyboard, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the button that opened it.

Restore appends a version.
Restoring announces the exact restored copy, and the versions JSON shows a new newest version with `restored_from` set and every earlier version unchanged.

New version appears live in a second tab.
The author's second tab adds the new version to `Versions` and updates `Latest version` within the published live delay and without a reload.

Compare outlasts notices.
While the compare, unsaved step text or a drop preview is open, an expiring `Editor status` notice or an arriving question leaves them open and unchanged, and an older notice timer never clears a newer message.

Forms and compare look.
Forms are adjoining outlined cells with sentence-case labels and square corners, and the version compare is two butted fields, older on the darker bone and newer on bone, with thick side bars marking changes.

Forking journey.
The `reader` forks the world's `public` guide by keyboard, sees the credit on the fork, and finds the fork on their dashboard after reload, while the author's open page shows the fork count live.

Fork dialog by keyboard.
`Fork guide` opens its dialog by keyboard with Tab wrapping and Escape returning focus, and its confirm button creates the fork and opens the fork's editor.

Fork credit and JSON.
The fork page shows the exact credit copy with a link to the source guide, and the fork API answers with the published `forked_from` JSON.

Fork count updates live.
The source guide's open reader page changes `Fork count` to the published text within the published live delay and without a reload.

Fork stays independent.
Later edits, saved versions, withdrawal or deletion of the source never change the fork's steps, model or credit, and the fork's reader page still loads its stage.

Forks shelf and empty shelves.
The fork sits under `Forks` on the owner's dashboard after reload and in a new session, and an account with nothing on a shelf sees that shelf's exact empty sentence.

Private guides cannot be forked.
Forking the world's `private` guide as `reader` answers the not-found answer and creates no fork row.

Co-editing journey.
Author and co-author in one draft see each other's presence, merge edits to different fields, and settle a same-field change through the conflict dialog by keyboard, in two browser contexts.

People editing shows who and where.
`People editing` lists the other person and their step within the published live delay, and at 375x812 it sits directly above the `Editor panes` tabs.

Presence drops after the tab closes.
When a co-editor's tab closes, their entry leaves `People editing` within `PRESENCE_GRACE_SECONDS` plus the published live delay.

Different fields merge.
Edits by two people to different fields of one draft both appear in both contexts and in the working-copy API, with no dialog.

Same-field conflict dialog.
A same-field change opens the `Edit conflict` alertdialog with the exact copy naming the other person, both values shown, and `Keep mine` and `Take theirs` reachable by keyboard with Tab wrapping.

Conflict choices store the chosen value.
`Keep mine` and `Take theirs` each give the published stored value in the working-copy API, in both contexts, and their exact `Editor status` announcement.

Stale saves are refused.
A version save with an old base answers the published 409 body and overwrites nothing, and in the editor it shows the stale copy, keeps the typed text, and opens the compare of both sides.

Questions journey.
`newcomer` is refused, confirms through the delivered message and asks about step 4 by keyboard, the author's open dashboard gets the question live, and the reader sees the answer live.

Unconfirmed account refused.
A signed-in unconfirmed account pressing `Ask the author` gets the exact refusal copy in `Guide status` and a `Resend confirmation` button, and upload, save, like and ask answer the published 403 body.

Confirmation message from Mailpit.
The delivered message has the published sender, subject and link, a resend voids the earlier token, an expired token is refused after `CONFIRM_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` on `short-limits`, and no page or API response ever carries the token.

Ask dialog by keyboard.
`Ask the author` opens its dialog by keyboard at the current step, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it, Escape returns focus to the button, and sending adds the question.

Question reaches the open dashboard.
A new question appears on the author's open dashboard within the published live delay and without a reload, announced with the exact `Question alerts` copy, and none are lost or repeated after a dropped connection.

Literal text and live answers.
Question and answer text with markup characters shows exactly as typed with no interpreted element, and the author's answer appears on the reader's open page live with its `Question alerts` copy.

Limits tell when to try again.
The `short-limits` instance refuses the third question in its window with 429, `Retry-After` and the exact copy in `Ask status`, and failed sign-ins and resends meet their published limits the same way.

Discovery journey.
A signed-out visitor searches by words and tags and pages through results, then a signed-in owner reorders a collection by keyboard and a reader likes a guide while the author's page updates live.

Search updates in place.
Typing in `Search guides` updates the results and huge count in place, with no reload, after the published delay, and announces the exact count copy in `Search status`.

Tags by keyboard.
In the `Filter by tag` combobox, arrow keys and Enter add a tag, each tag has a named remove button, and Backspace in the empty field removes the last tag, with results updating each time.

Search lives in the address.
The query and tags live in the address and survive a reload, and private, draft and withdrawn guides never appear in results.

Paging and search limits.
`Load more` continues from a cursor without repeating or skipping a guide while new guides are published, the API caps page size, and over-long queries and too many tags answer 422 with their exact `Search status` copy.

Collection order by keyboard.
On a collection page the owner moves a focused guide with Alt+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowDown, hears the exact `Collection status` copy, and sees the same order after a reload.

Likes count once and live.
`Like` toggles `aria-pressed`, each account counts once, and the author's open page shows the exact `Like count` text within the published live delay.

Dashboard and search look.
The dashboard is a stack of full-bleed shelves in the published colours with large display headings on one left edge and big type rows rather than cards, and search shows results on bone with the count set huge.

Embed and sound journey.
An embedder opens a step address on the embed route, sees it settled and read-only, moves between steps, presses the sound button on and off, and checks a withdrawn guide's page, at desktop and phone sizes.

Embed opens settled and read-only.
`/embed/<slug>?step=3` shows step 3's settled hooks and final parts cost on first paint, with the published controls and no edit, like, fork or question control.

Embed ignores the session.
The embed page looks identical to signed-in and signed-out contexts, sets no cookie, shows no account name, and carries the published frame-ancestors headers while every other page carries the other published value.

Sound stays off until pressed.
Before the first press of `Workshop sound` no audio context, source or gain exists, every new page load starts off, and `sound=off` hides the button.

Sound presses set the master gain.
The first press starts one looping generated source through one master gain at the published level with `aria-pressed="true"`, and the next press sets that gain to 0 with `aria-pressed="false"`.

Publish states reach the embed.
`Publish` and `Withdraw` in the editor follow the published guide states with their copy and rejections, and the embed and reader show the exact withdrawn copy until the guide is published again, with private, draft and unknown guides showing the not-found page.

Embed fits a phone.
At 375x812 the embed view has no sideways overflow, the numbered `Parts` list replaces callouts, and every control is at least 44 by 44 px.
`/app/run.json` exists with string `install`, `build` and `serve` commands and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at the repository root lists every shipped package and bundled font with its licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`, or the lockfile's non-dev group).
Shipped packages and bundled fonts use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1 licences; shipped packages means the production dependency tree as in IF-02.
Postgres and MinIO are the only datastores, with no other database, queue or cache service and no state in server files.
The app makes no third-party request in the browser or on the server beyond the listed services: no CDN, remote font, remote image, remote model or analytics.
No service worker is registered anywhere in the source.
A lockfile is committed and the seeded dev service configuration stays unchanged.
